sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Income-Generating Real Estate Property Portfolio Trust (REIT)

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama-European Union Central America Free Trade Agreement
Panama-Netherlands Bilateral Investment Treaty and Double Tax Agreement

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 23 of 27 April 2015 (AML/CFT) as amended; Executive Decree No. 363 of 2016 (PEP and sanctions obligations); Law No. 52 of 2016 on Tax Transparency; Executive Decree No. 420 of 24 April 2017 establishing the Beneficial Ownership Registry; and Unified Decree No. 1 of 2019 implementing the Financial Superintendency for non-financial obliged subjects.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public / Embassy of the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the Panama Resident Agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the jurisdiction of the principal

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter and Proof of Source of Funds
Certificate of Incorporation of corporate shareholder(s)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry of jurisdiction of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all beneficial owners, directors, and senior managers against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council sanctions lists, the EU consolidated sanctions list, and the Panamanian national list maintained by the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF) under Executive Decree 363/2016. Positive hits require enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, and filing of a suspicious transaction report to the UAF within statutory timeframes.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá (Oficina Administrativa), online at www.registro-publico.gob.pa
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be expressed in Latin-script characters, using Spanish, English, or another recognized language; if the intended name derives from a non-Latin script, an officially certified transliteration into the Latin alphabet is required. The name must end with or include the suffix 'S.A.' or 'Sociedad Anónima' or an accepted equivalent such as 'Corp.', 'Inc.', or 'Ltd.', provided it is not identical or deceptively similar to an existing registered entity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed name, the applicant may file a written reconsideration petition with the Dirección General de Registro within five business days from notification, attaching evidence of legitimate interest or trade usage. If reconsideration is denied, an administrative appeal may be lodged before the Superior Administrative Court within ten business days from the date of notification of the denial.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office (use of the resident agent's address for registered office purposes) is generally permissible for a holding or passive real estate entity, but a REIT engaged in active property management, collection of rents, or investor-facing activities must maintain a physical office in Panama or appoint a local property manager to satisfy commercial substance expectations.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff set by the Registry of Public Register fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille of corporate documents (including translation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary Public and Ministry of External Relations (or authorised apostille officer)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Panama notary tariff and apostille fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Incorporation legal fee — drafting of articles of incorporation and bylaws
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for standard S.A. formation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Panama resident agency licensed by MICI
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market-standard annual retainer for resident agent services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO registration filing and initial due diligence
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Resident Agent / Registro Público de Panamá
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee for beneficial ownership registry filing and agent administrative charge

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC screening and PEP check fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Flat fee per UBO / shareholder covering OFAC, UN, EU, and local UAF database checks

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostilled bank reference letter procurement (if corporate shareholder)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank service charge and apostille processing fee

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 32 de 1927 (General Corporation Law of the Republic of Panama), as amended, Book II, Chapter I, Articles 1-10, 14-15, 25-26 and 31.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Departamento de Inscripción de Sociedades Anónimas, Acting with a Panamanian Notary Public.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (Public Deed of Incorporation), followed by Calificación and Inscripción; the registered output is the Certificado de Inscripción.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required under Law 32 of 1927; the articles may fix a nominal capital (e.g. USD 10,000) at the incorporators' discretion. There is no escrow, pre-funding, or capital levy condition precedent to registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY], S.A. WHEREAS the Articles of Incorporation were registered with the Public Registry of Panama; IT IS HEREBY RESOLVED: 1. The subscriptions to the authorized shares set out in the subscription list are accepted; share certificates shall be allotted. 2. The registered office is established at [Street Address], Panama City, Republic of Panama. 3. The following officers are appointed: President, Secretary and Treasurer, with powers and duties per the by-laws. 4. The President and Secretary are authorized jointly to open bank accounts, sign contracts and effect all government filings. APPROVED unanimously this [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Personas, via PanamáEmprende (Ventanilla Única de Inversión)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three alternative corporate names through the official PanamáEmprende portal or in person to the Public Registry. The Registry performs an exact and phonetic search and issues the name availability certificate ('Certificado de Búsqueda y Reserva de Nombre') which must be retained for the incorporation deed.
required_dossiers: Identification of the incorporating shareholder or authorized attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is denied because it is identical or confusingly similar, file a new search with modified alternatives, or appeal to the Director General of the Registry within five business days attaching evidence of distinctiveness.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of the Public Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Republic of Panama (Notaría de Circuito) acting with local licensed counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Escritura Pública (or Pacto Social) containing corporate name, registered office, corporate term, authorized capital and share classes, board size, and by-laws. The incorporators must execute the deed before a Panamanian Notary, who authenticates signatures and stamps the deed for presentation to the Public Registry.
required_dossiers: Passport or identity card copies of incorporators and initial directors
Draft Articles of Incorporation and legal review
Power of attorney if execution is by attorney-in-fact
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notary observes defects (e.g. incomplete capital clauses, missing parties), the deed is corrected and re-executed. The notarial fee will be recalculated and no material setback occurs if amended prior to submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing and Registration with the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Departamento de Inscripción de Sociedades (Ficha Electrónica)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the notarized Escritura Pública together with the registration fee receipt to the Corporations Branch. The Registry performs a legality review (calificación), digitalizes the record, and effectuates the inscription. The issuance of the Certificado de Inscripción completes the statutory formation.
required_dossiers: Receipt of official registry fee payment
Cover sheet and sworn signatures if required by Registry rules
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Upon receiving an observation, the corporate counsel must submit a written response within five business days; if the registry upholds the rejection, the applicant may re-file or bring a judicial appeal before the Third Chamber of the Supreme Court of Justice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution, Share Allotment and Statutory Books
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene a board meeting, adopt the first board resolution approving share subscriptions, fixing the registered office and appointing officers. Open and stamp the statutory books (share ledger, minutes book, and board decision book) with the Public Registry, if required, and issue the final share certificates.
required_dossiers: Statutory books (libro de acciones y actas)
Subscription list and capital payment evidence (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Public Registry declines to stamp any statutory book for non-compliance, conform the minutes to the registry's requirements and resubmit within three business days; the corporate directors may also ratify the amendment informally.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Municipal Operation Notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, and the Municipalidad de Panamá (PanamáEmprende)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, file the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) application electronically or in person, providing the corporate documentation and identifying the legal representative. If the corporation occupies a physical office, complete the municipal 'Aviso de Operación' / business license at the local municipality's single window.
required_dossiers: Identity card/passport of the legal representative
Proof of registered office address (lease or utility bill)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI suspends the RUC process, the taxpayer may provide the missing documentation and request acceleration; any municipal license objection is cured by submitting an updated lease, zoning certificate, or structural safety inspection report.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Superintendencia del Mercado de Valores de Panamá (SMV) for REIT qualification; Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) for the commercial operating license; Municipalidad de Panamá for the local business permit.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorización de Sociedad de Inversión Inmobiliaria (REIT License) and Aviso de Operación / Business License for Real Estate Portfolio Activity

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente de Panamá (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I (Environmental Registration) for passive income-generating property portfolio; Category II (Preliminary EIA) or Category III (Full EIA) only if the REIT undertakes construction, major renovation, or development of the underlying real estate.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater is generated at the REIT level; each property must obtain its own wastewater and atmospheric discharge permits. Discharges must meet Panama's national effluent limits (pH 6.0-8.5, BOD5 ≤ 30 mg/L, TSS ≤ 50 mg/L) and air emissions must satisfy ambient air quality standards; any volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions are abated by vapor recovery or carbon adsorption, with release records maintained for MiAMBIENTE inspection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Each operating property must obtain the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá fire safety certificate, municipal structural and occupancy inspection, and SINAPROC evacuation/emergency compliance where applicable. The REIT's own office must register with MITRADEL for occupational health and safety and obtain the workplace clearance before employees are stationed.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF); tax administration and filing portal: DGI e-Tax electronic services platform and the Sistema de Facturación Electrónica (SFE) portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Sociedad Anónima must: (1) incorporate through a licensed resident agent and register the corporate deed with the Registro Público de Panamá; (2) maintain a registered office in Panama and obtain the municipal Aviso de Operación; (3) appoint a local fiscal representative (representante fiscal) and file the Formulario de Solicitud de Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) with the DGI, attaching the certificate of incorporation, bylaws, shareholder and officer records, and proof of registered address; (4) upon issuance of the RUC/NIT, complete the ITBMS (VAT) registration and, where applicable, employer registration; and (5) activate the DGI e-Tax digital certificate and SFE electronic-invoicing enrolment. Non-resident shareholders are expressly permitted and no local shareholding is required; the resident agent and fiscal representative remain the statutory service and filing nexus.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not provide a US-style 'check-the-box' or elective pass-through regime; every Sociedad Anónima is an entity-level taxpayer, liable only on Panamanian-source income. Available statutory elections include: (a) the territorial-source taxation default, with complete exclusion of foreign-source income; (b) optional consolidated income tax filing for economically linked companies subject to prior DGI authorization; (c) the simplified small-taxpayer quota method for ITBMS where annual turnover is within statutory limits; and (d) the special capital-market regimes for SMV-regulated investment funds, trusts, and real-estate investment vehicles, which may achieve tax-neutral distribution treatment upon fulfillment of licensing and public-registry conditions. Hybrid mismatch elections are not recognized under the Código Fiscal; transfer-pricing documentation follows BEPS-aligned rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto a la Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS) — Panamanian value-added tax (VAT) levied on the transfer of goods, provision of services, and imports within Panamanian territory, administered by the DGI.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Panama imposes no monetary exemption threshold: any person habitually carrying on taxable commercial activity in Panamanian territory must obtain a RUC and register as an ITBMS collector upon commencement of operations. Taxpayers with gross annual taxable turnover not exceeding B/.36,000 (Balboas, pegged 1:1 to the US dollar) may elect the simplified small-taxpayer quota regime; above that threshold, full monthly ITBMS return filing, SFE electronic invoicing, and input-tax credit accounting are mandatory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All active ITBMS taxpayers must issue electronic invoices through DGI-certified accounting software or the SFE web portal. Each invoice is transmitted to the DGI in near-real time, validated, and returned with a unique digital stamp and QR code (código de validación) that must appear on the invoice delivered to the buyer; unvalidated invoices are not tax-deductible by the recipient. The e-invoicing mandate is phased by taxpayer category under successive DGI resolutions, with full rejection-and-correction workflows integrated into the e-Tax environment.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% ITBMS rate applies where: (i) tangible goods are physically exported from Panama under customs supervision; (ii) services qualify as offshore services, being rendered to a beneficiary not domiciled in Panama and not consumed or commercially exploited within Panamanian territory; and (iii) the exporter is a registered ITBMS taxpayer issuing valid electronic invoices. For this REIT entity, rental income from real estate situated in Panama does NOT qualify for export zero-rating, because the situs of the property constitutes Panamanian-source consumption; zero-rating remains available only for cross-border advisory or management services to non-resident investors and for tangible goods exported abroad. Input ITBMS attributable to zero-rated transactions may be offset or recovered as saldos a favor through the DGI refund mechanism.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación) filed and cleared through the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA) electronic module
Commercial invoice, in Spanish or English, expressly stating the ITBMS zero-rated (0%) nature of the transaction
Original Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or multimodal transport document evidencing physical departure from Panamanian territory
Packing list and, where applicable, certificate of origin
Bank credit advice or Inward Remittance Certificate proving collection of the export proceeds from the foreign buyer
For offshore services: signed cross-border service contract and tax-residence certificate of the non-resident recipient
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Panama is dollarized and maintains no separate exchange-control repatriation regime, so the 180-day period represents the DGI-accepted evidentiary window for crediting export proceeds to a Panamanian bank account; the bank credit advice is the controlling proof. The DGI, in coordination with the ANA, may retrospectively reopen export zero-rating claims for up to six years. Fraudulent, backdated, or materially defective export documentation triggers: (i) re-levy of ITBMS at the 7% standard rate; (ii) statutory late-payment surcharge and interest; (iii) administrative fines generally ranging from one to three times the omitted tax; (iv) clawback (inadmissibility) of related input credits; and (v) criminal tax-fraud liability for the legal representatives and fiscal representative, with imprisonment of two to five years under the Código Fiscal and Law 8 of 2010, as amended. Missing ANA clearance or inward-remittance evidence defeats the zero-rating claim and converts the transaction into an uncollected taxable supply at the standard rate.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) — banking regulator and de facto monetary authority under Panama's full-dollarization regime; Banco Nacional de Panamá — fiscal agent and state-owned settlement bank; Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) — fiscal and monetary policy coordination. Panama has no currency-issuing central bank; the United States Federal Reserve System serves as the effective provider of base money.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama operates a fully dollarized monetary system: the US Dollar is legal tender for all banking, clearing, and contractual obligations, and the Balboa exists only as sub-dollar coinage at a fixed 1:1 parity. Convertibility is total and unrestricted for both current account transactions (rents, service fees, interest, lease income) and capital account transactions (equity injections, redemption of participations, repatriation of sale proceeds). There are no exchange-rate bands, no prior FX licensing requirements, and no foreign-exchange control statute. Profit remittance hurdles are exclusively fiscal rather than FX-related: dividends distributed by a Panamanian Sociedad Anónima out of Panamanian-source taxable income bear a 10% dividend tax, which may be withheld by the corporation or paid as a prepayment, and remittances of taxable dividend amounts require production of DGI payment certifications. Distributions made from foreign-source income under Panama's territorial tax principle are exempt from dividend taxation. No additional FX approval is required; the REIT may remit USD directly through any SBP-licensed bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Panama imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio. Exporters, cross-border service providers, and REITs receiving foreign-source consideration (including sale proceeds from overseas properties and non-Panamanian rental income) may freely retain, convert, or disburse USD, EUR, or other convertible currencies without governmental intervention. There is no prescribed repatriation timeline and no obligation to report foreign receipts to the DGI except under standard AML/CFT reporting rules, namely UAF currency transaction reports for transactions at or above USD 10,000 and any suspicious-activity reporting.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating for principal treasury operations: LOW. Legal constraints: (i) foreign offshore EMIs hold no Panamanian banking license and cannot lawfully receive core operating deposits from a Panama-domiciled REIT without breaching banking intermediation restrictions under Decree Law 9 of 1998; (ii) the SBP authorizes payment services exclusively through locally incorporated payment entities under its fintech regulatory framework (SBP Agreement 004-2022), and a foreign EMI lacks membership in Panama's ACH clearing house and direct access to the local SWIFT correspondent network; (iii) funds held at a foreign EMI remain outside SBP prudential supervision and Panama's deposit-protection coverage; (iv) for escrow-linked REIT capital commitments, counterparties and settling banks will not treat EMI account statements as proof of cleared funds. Ancillary viability: MEDIUM — a foreign EMI may be employed solely for tenant pre-collection in niche cross-border corridors on the condition that balances are swept daily to the local tier-1 operational account; such arrangements must be disclosed in the REIT's AML/CFT compliance program and carry elevated money-laundering risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory for most tier-1 institutions. SBP due-diligence rules (Agreement 002-2013, as amended) require legal-entity clients to be represented by a natural person whose identity is verified face-to-face; banks have adopted only partial remote digital onboarding for non-resident corporates. In practice, the REIT's resident Panamanian director or the holder of a registered power of attorney must attend an in-person account-opening interview, and beneficial owners must provide passports notarized by a Panamanian notary. Remote opening is occasionally permitted for low-risk structures where the UBO already maintains a senior personal banking relationship with the same institution; otherwise a virtual interview followed by courier-delivered original documentation is accepted only on a documented exception basis.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ownership — non-resident ultimate beneficial owners holding the REIT through a Panama private interest foundation (PIF), nominee shareholder, or trust arrangement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete beneficial-ownership attestation disclosing 100% of natural persons; certified copy of the PIF deed or trust instrument; apostilled passports of all UBOs; sworn source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements; current certificado de persona jurídica from the Registro Público; tax-registration certificate (Aviso de Operación); and completed officers' and directors' identification forms.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lumpy capital injections for property acquisitions funded from mixed or third-party sources, triggering high-value alerts above USD 500,000.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-resolved capital contribution plan; notarized shareholders' contribution resolutions; 24-month traceable bank-transaction history of the funding shareholder; executed promise-of-sale contract with closing schedule; certified title search from the Registro Público; independent fair-market appraisal prepared by an SMV-licensed appraiser; and a legal opinion from Panamanian counsel confirming that the equity contribution is not subject to Panamanian source tax.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Recurring inbound tenant and lease payments creating a multi-party payment pattern through the operational account without a documented lease registry.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed and publicly registered lease agreements for each property unit; tenant identity records including PEP screening results; updated rent roll; property-management agreement appointing a Panamanian administrator; and a compliance-approved whitelist of recurring tenant remitters established with the bank's AML unit before the first credit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound dividend distributions to offshore shareholders in FATF-grey-listed or perceived non-cooperative tax jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: DGI dividend-tax payment receipts; audited financial statements evidencing distributable retained earnings; board distribution resolution; territorial-source analysis by Panamanian tax counsel demonstrating that distributions utilise foreign-source or non-taxable reserves; and maintained economic-substance evidence, including a local administration office, physical premises, and valid registrations, to rebut treaty-abuse and beneficial-ownership challenges.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound routing relies on direct SWIFT MT103 credits to the REIT's operational account at a tier-1 SBP-licensed bank. Panama maintains no statutory purpose-code system; remitters should nevertheless state in SWIFT Field 70: 'Equity contribution to REIT capital base — Panamanian territorial exemption', referencing the shareholder number and REIT registration file. Verification protocols: (i) currency-transaction reporting to the UAF for any credit of USD 10,000 or more; (ii) enhanced due diligence requiring source-of-funds evidence for credits above USD 30,000; (iii) notarized contribution agreements or funds-comfort letters for credits above USD 500,000; and (iv) confirmation that the originating institution is licensed in a FATF-compliant jurisdiction. The receiving bank must also verify authorized signatories and corporate-sealing against its mandate records prior to crediting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements for property purchases, construction disbursements, and income distributions execute predominantly via SWIFT MT103 through each Panamanian bank's New York correspondent (CHIPS), reflecting Panama's USD-based clearing infrastructure; large-value local payments may settle intraday through the national automated clearing house (Cámara de Compensación Automatizada). Construction and development disbursements are routed under irrevocable commercial letters of credit issued per UCP 600 by the tier-1 Panamanian bank against drawdown certificates, invoices, and lien waivers. Escrow disbursements follow the conditions precedent of the purchase contract and are released only upon confirmation of title transfer at the Registro Público. Outbound DGI-taxed dividends must cite the tax-payment reference in SWIFT Field 72 where the receiving jurisdiction or correspondent bank requires tax attestation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (EUR/USD, GBP/USD, CHF/USD) executed with SBP-licensed counterparty banks
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) hedging EUR- or CAD-denominated REIT debt obligations
OTC vanilla FX options (purchased protective puts and calls) with licensed bank counterparties

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for exposures in restricted-currency markets such as CNY, ARS, and CLP, executed offshore with qualified international banks under the REIT's documented treasury policy
Plain-vanilla USD interest-rate swaps aligned with the asset-liability management of the trust

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by March 31 for the calendar fiscal year; newly incorporated entities remit the first annual tax within 30 days of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A 5% monthly surcharge and interest accrue on late payments; two successive unpaid annual periods may trigger administrative strike-off from the Public Registry of Panama.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Confirmation (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Registro de Beneficiarios Finales, Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by June 30 and within 30 days of any shareholding transfer, issuance, or change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing suspends issuance of good-standing certificates and exposes the entity to administrative penalties under Law 23 of 2015; repeated default may lead to strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Ledger Sealing and Register Legalization (Legalización de Libros y Registros)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry of Panama)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after each annual shareholders' general meeting, and no later than June 30 for a calendar-year company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors and officers may face personal liability for false records; the Public Registry may reject certified corporate documents and issue a negative standing notation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is automatically required for a passive Panama Sociedad Anónima. Audit becomes mandatory when the entity is a publicly listed company, a licensed financial or trust company, or is classified by the DGI as a Gran Contribuyente (global gross revenue above USD 1,000,000). For a REIT vehicle holding real estate passively, audit is required only if such a threshold or license applies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (including IFRS for SMEs, as approved by the Panamanian Chamber of Accountants) is the applicable framework; entities may also use Panamanian GAAP for micro-entities, but accounting records must be maintained in accordance with the books mandates of Law 32 of 1927.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each year, the registered agent must file a sworn declaration with the DGI Beneficial Owner Registry confirming the full chain of shareholding, including any transfers of registered shares and the custodied status of any bearer shares. The confirmation must be executed by the legal representative and updated without delay after any change in ownership, capital increase, or transfer event.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - USD 8,000 per interview if audit becomes mandatory or is voluntarily engaged

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Panama-source income only; 25% flat corporate rate reduced to 15% for net taxable income not exceeding USD 1,500,000 under Law 8 of 2010; no tax on foreign-source revenue; full depreciation deduction on Panamanian real estate and ordinary local operating costs; no municipal or regional surcharge on income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 300 (Declaración de Renta) submitted electronically through the DGI e-Tax portal (e-tax.dgi.gob.pa)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within four months after the end of the fiscal year; for calendar-year taxpayers, due by 31 March of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identifies the taxable period covered by the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the calendar year corresponding to the twelve-month period; foreign-currency amounts must be converted to Panamanian Balboa/USD at the official exchange rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2: Identification Data (RUC, Name, Entity Type)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer RUC, registered legal name, address, and domicile.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Panamanian RUC obtained from the local registered agent; a foreign tax identification number is insufficient.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross income from Panamanian real estate leases, property services, and other locally sourced activities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all income from Panama real estate held through the REIT; exclude foreign dividends and interest unless effectively connected to a Panamanian permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses directly related to local revenue, including mortgage interest, maintenance, depreciation, payroll, and professional fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach contracts and invoices; expenses must be registered with the DGI and have been incurred for generating Panamanian-source income; transfer-pricing adjustments apply to related-party services.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Panama-source gross income less deductible expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Negative amounts create a deductible NOL carryforward for up to five years; foreign-source losses may not be offset.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory corporate income tax computed on net taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the flat 25% rate; the reduced 15% rate applies only if net taxable income is within the USD 1,500,000 threshold. No territorial extension to foreign income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for advance income tax payments and third-party withholdings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim tenant withholding certificates and advance payments made via the local registered agent; credits must be evidenced by DGI forms.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8: Net Tax Due or Refund
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final balance after prepayments and credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay the net balance by the statutory deadline via the DGI e-Tax portal; no wire refund issued unless the REIT has a deposit account in Panama and a clear RUC status.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: monthly surcharge of 1% of the tax due, up to 25%, plus annual interest of 10%; administrative fines from USD 50 to USD 5,000 per unfiled return; non-filing blocks issuance of the RUC certificate and prevents public registry operations. Reckless understatement triggers a 30% penalty on the tax understated.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on gross dividends paid to all shareholders; reduced to 5% final withholding when the distributing corporation has paid the normal 25% corporate income tax on the profits underlying the distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced rate under Panama's double tax agreement, the non-resident shareholder must file a written application with the DGI attaching: (i) a sworn claim for treaty relief, (ii) the Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by the shareholder's home jurisdiction for the relevant year, (iii) an affidavit of beneficial ownership, and (iv) the applicable DTA article and residence analysis. DGI confirmation or a valid self-assessment is required before the paying entity may apply the reduced treaty withholding; submission to the local payer must occur no later than the dividend distribution date.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: 5% statutory withholding for interest payments to non-residents, except interest on loans from foreign financial institutions not conducting business in Panama, which is usually exempt. Royalties: 20% statutory withholding on payments for patents, trademarks, know-how, and copyrights used in Panama; treaty-eligible recipients may reduce royalties to 10% or 15% depending on the DTA. Panama-source technical assistance fees to non-residents are generally taxed at 12.5% unless reduced by treaty.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 2,000,000 in aggregate related-party transactions in a fiscal year; a Local File is required when related-party revenue exceeds this threshold. A Master File is required when the Panama entity belongs to a multinational group with consolidated worldwide turnover exceeding USD 50 million. The REIT must also file Form 210 (Related-Party Transactions Information Return) with the DGI for any covered transaction.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Regulations (Law 78 of 2019) apply to any entity undertaking 'relevant activities', including a Real Estate Investment Trust holding Panamanian property. The REIT must show: (i) management and direction in Panama, (ii) adequate physical premises, (iii) qualified employees and payroll, and (iv) core income-generating activity in Panama. A full ESR information return is due within twelve months of fiscal year-end; failure to satisfy ESR creates a conclusive presumption of shell status.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of Panamanian rental income from the Form 300, fabricated deductions, or use of shell vehicles to disguise local real-estate revenue as foreign-source income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of up to 200% of evaded tax, monthly surcharges, and criminal penalties of 2 to 5 years imprisonment under Law 70 of 2019; the tax liability becomes enforceable against all group assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for civil restitution where they signed the false return; the DGI may impose travel bans when the unpaid tax exceeds USD 10,000, and criminal proceedings carry imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Economic Substance Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: REIT lacking physical office, local employees, and proper books despite owning several high-value Panamanian properties; management conducted entirely from a foreign registered agent's desk under an umbrella arrangement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ESR non-compliance penalties up to USD 50,000 for false filings; the DGI can dissolve the entity and disallow treaty withholding benefits; profits may be reclassified and taxed at 25% plus 50% surcharge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced for shell misuse; directors may be disqualified from forming new Panamanian entities, their shares frozen, and they may face 3 to 5 years imprisonment for breach of Economic Substance Regulations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the REIT to receive cash rental payments or real-estate sale proceeds from politically exposed persons without completing beneficial-owner due diligence, maintaining no AML records, or structuring payments to avoid the USD 10,000 transparency threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines under Law 23 of 2015 of up to USD 5,000,000; criminal money-laundering sanctions from 5 to 15 years imprisonment; assets linked to illicit activity may be confiscated.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are criminally responsible for willful failure to apply AML controls; travel bans and asset freezes are imposed, and the corporate veil is pierced to the extent of illicit proceeds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Fatal Red Flags
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling Panamanian real estate to a related foreign trust at a substantial undervalue, or paying inflated property-management fees to an offshore affiliate to move taxable profits out of Panama.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DGI may reassess taxable income using the arm's-length standard, apply a 25% tax on the adjustment, charge a 10% penalty, and impose monthly interest from the original due date; criminal referral for a false statement is possible.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed the transactional documents with knowledge of the non-arm's-length price are jointly liable for the additional tax and penalty; civil suits for restitution by minority shareholders may also pierce the veil.
